title: A moving light clock ticks slower
lede: A light pulse bounces between two mirrors. Left: the clock at rest. Right: the same clock moving at speed v, seen from the rest frame. Light has the same speed in both.
notice: In the moving clock the pulse travels a diagonal, longer than the straight gap. Light cannot go faster, so each tick lasts longer.
The path per tick divided by the gap, solved from the geometry, equals gamma = 1/sqrt(1 - v²/c²), and so does the ratio of tick lengths.
The mirrors are narrower when moving, which is length contraction along the motion. The gap between them does not change.
hint: Drag the speed slider. Press Pause to study a tick.
